findings.source_passage: When did my heart get a vote on this? / When I said it had one.
findings.why_it_matters: The source's 'When I said it had one' is a sharp, characterful assertion that defines Heather's bossy warmth; the draft's 'When I gave it one' softens the declarative authority and loses the rhythm of the original.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'When I said it had one' verbatim — it's a two-line comic beat that reads as a mini-signature of Heather's voice.

findings.source_passage: She dragged me to my butt-mark in the dirt and arranged us so we faced each other.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 10, after Heather says 'Maybe that's it'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Butt-mark in the dirt' is a register-defining comic detail that grounds the narrator's self-deprecating voice; the draft's 'exact butt-print I'd left' is close but loses 'arranged us so we faced each other,' which sets up the ritual-intimacy of the portal-opening scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'arranged us so we faced each other' — the staging detail is small but the blocking matters for the ensuing moment.

findings.source_passage: She stepped forward and looked at me before she jerked her head toward the portal. 'Well? What are you waiting for?' I smiled and gave her a tight hug. We parted and I could see a few tears in her eyes.
findings.source_locator: after 'I don't know,' before 'Go on. You shouldn't keep a dragon waiting.'
findings.why_it_matters: The source specifies Miriam smiles before the hug, and that they 'parted' with tears visible — a beat-by-beat emotional choreography that earns the farewell; the draft collapses it to 'I hugged her tight. Tears glimmered,' losing the initiating smile and the mutual parting.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sequence: Miriam smiles first, then hugs, then they part and she sees Heather's tears — three distinct emotional micro-beats the draft compresses into one.

findings.source_passage: Apuleius turned to one of the gray-cloaked men. 'I will escort My Lady to My Lord.' The gray cloaked man whipped his head up so quickly his hood fell backward to reveal his astonished face. 'But Father Apuleius—'
findings.source_locator: after 'We must get you to him immediately,' before the gold-cloaked speaker
findings.why_it_matters: The hood-falling-back detail and the subordinate's protest ('But Father Apuleius—') establish the mild insubordination Apuleius is committing and make the gold-cloaked elder's blessing more meaningful; their absence flattens the social stakes of the exchange.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the gray-cloaked man's interrupted objection and the hood-falling detail in one sentence before the gold-cloaked elder speaks.

findings.source_passage: 'Please forgive me—' The one in the gold cloak raised his hand and shook his head. 'Do not concern yourself with apologies. We all would risk our cloaks for our lords.'
findings.source_locator: after 'Father Apuleius—' protest, before 'Now to the skies'
findings.why_it_matters: 'We all would risk our cloaks for our lords' is a world-building grace note that characterises the sage community's ethic; its absence reduces the gold-cloaked elder to a functional plot-greaser.
findings.suggested_fix: Add back the 'Do not concern yourself with apologies. We all would risk our cloaks for our lords' line — it is brief and tonally distinctive.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium findings around voice flattening in the Heather dialogue and the farewell scene, plus two low-severity omissions in the sage exchange, but none individually severe enough to require regeneration.
